structured_output.summary: The forEach skeleton follows the spec order (ToObject, LengthOfArrayLike, IsCallable check, index loop, Call with three arguments, return undefined). However, two abrupt completions are mishandled. HasProperty errors are discarded with unwrap_or(false), where the spec uses `?`. Get errors are replaced with Value::Undefined and the callback is then invoked, where the spec propagates the throw. Both are swallowed errors and the Get case also fabricates a value. The change must not be merged as-is.

problems.question: swallows_errors
problems.issue: Line 22: `has_property(agent, o, &pk).unwrap_or(false)` discards any throw completion from HasProperty. Spec step 5.b is `Let kPresent be ? HasProperty(O, Pk).` and the error must propagate with `?`.

problems.question: swallows_errors
problems.issue: Lines 26-30: `match get(agent, o, &pk) { Ok(v) => v, Err(_) => Value::Undefined }` swallows a throw from Get. Spec step 5.c.i is `Let kValue be ? Get(O, Pk).`; the error must propagate and the callback must not run.

problems.question: made_up_results
problems.issue: Lines 28-29: when Get throws, the code substitutes `Value::Undefined` as the element value and then calls the callback with it (line 32). This fabricates a value the spec never produces. The comment 'treat as a hole' is wrong: the spec treats only HasProperty=false as a hole.

problems.question: contradicts_spec
problems.issue: Same as the two swallowed-error items: step 5.b and 5.c.i both require `?` propagation. The implementation calls the callback after a Get throw and continues the loop after a HasProperty throw, which is observably different from the spec.

structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Fix the error handling in for_each.rs. Step 5.b: `let k_present = has_property(agent, o, &pk)?;`. Step 5.c.i: `let k_value = get(agent, o, &pk)?;`. Delete the `Err(_) => Value::Undefined` fallback and its comment. Keep the rest of the structure: ToObject, LengthOfArrayLike, the IsCallable check before the loop, and Call with `?`. Do not add any special-casing. After the change, rerun the forEach test262 target and check that the 15.4.4.18-7-c-i-30/31 failures and the callbackfn-resize-arraybuffer failure are not caused by this code, since those are likely from the length or resize behaviour in the object model rather than from forEach itself.
